fresh_external_knowledge.question: Should an incremental UnifiedDB Pulse batch be allowed to publish against a projection head different from the basis against which the batch was computed?

sources.claim: SQLite WAL snapshot isolation rejects escalation from an old read snapshot to a write with SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT because writing from a stale snapshot would fork database history.
Differential-dataflow updates carry (data,time,diff), and write frontiers make logical-time completeness explicit; final content alone is not the full incremental-state identity.
MVCC semantics are defined over a database snapshot/version, reinforcing that consistency is tied to a versioned basis rather than only current row values.

fresh_external_knowledge.fusion: External evidence supports the current Pulse recovery falsifier's fail-closed direction: S2 publication should be causally bound to the exact projection basis/head used to derive the batch. A content-ABA fix is necessary but not sufficient if from-epoch/generation identity is discarded before publication.
fresh_external_knowledge.strongest_counterhypothesis: Checking only monotonically increasing target epochs is sufficient because omitted intermediate epochs cannot affect untouched projection segments.
fresh_external_knowledge.counterevidence: The active recovery falsifier constructs precisely the omitted-change case: an untouched-looking segment can be stale when the batch skips an unrepresented base-to-head interval. The external snapshot/version semantics make such a fail-open assumption structurally unsafe.
fresh_external_knowledge.required_gate: Before any S2 selection, require exact base binding (at minimum from_source_epoch/from_graph_epoch; preferably generation/head identity), fail closed before recompute/publication, then rerun crash/restart/replay plus sequential/full-rebuild equivalence.
